RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-CD6AF51965-72160
Requested Service: Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
Date of Notice: 2026-08-10
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-06

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), as described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-10 (Reference POC-CD6AF51965-72160). The stated reason for denial was: "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree, and I ask that Molina reverse this determination based on the clinical record summarized below.

1. The denial reason does not match my treatment history.

My orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Duval, has treated a documented full-thickness supraspinatus tear (1.8 cm, with grade 2 fatty atrophy on MRI dated 2026-07-06) that has caused progressive shoulder pain for 24 months. Prior to requesting surgery, I completed the following non-surgical treatment, which is documented in my chart:

- Supervised physical therapy targeting rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics: 8 weeks, 2026-05-23 through 2026-07-18, 24 visits completed (documented in the physical therapy discharge note);
- NSAID therapy for 8 months with inadequate relief;
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-21, which produced only 3 weeks of partial relief;
- Ongoing functional impairment despite this treatment, including inability to lift the arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side, and positive provocative testing with pain-limited range of motion on exam.

This is a well-documented, multi-modality trial of conservative care lasting substantially longer than the several-months window typically used to assess whether non-surgical management has failed, and it did not resolve my symptoms or the underlying structural tear.

2. Regarding the specific medical policy applied to this determination.

I have identified Molina's publicly posted clinical policy addressing shoulder arthroscopy, "Shoulder Arthroscopy Guidelines," Policy Number MCP-404 (Original Effective Date 6/9/2021). That document states: "This policy addresses arthroscopic procedures when performed as an elective, non-emergent technique for disease pathology that will cause progressive destruction. Please see MCG criteria for rotator cuff repair." By its own terms, MCP-404 does not contain the medical-necessity criteria for CPT 29827; Molina states that rotator cuff repair is instead evaluated under MCG guideline criteria.

I have not been able to obtain the text of that MCG criterion, and I am not quoting or asserting any specific MCG requirement here because I have not seen it. I note, however, that in the sections of MCP-404 that do set out Molina's conservative-care standard for other arthroscopic shoulder procedures (debridement and labral/SLAP repair), Molina requires: "Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration including at least two of the following as appropriate: Activity modification; Assistive devices (e.g., sling, splint, brace); Physical therapy; Physician or physical therapist-supervised therapeutic home exercise program which includes flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises; Prescription strength anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics; Intraarticular corticosteroid injection(s)." I offer this only as an illustration of the type of standard Molina applies to comparable shoulder procedures, not as the governing text for CPT 29827. My treatment history — 8 months of NSAIDs, an intra-articular corticosteroid injection, and 8 weeks/24 visits of supervised physical therapy over a 24-month symptomatic period — meets or exceeds this type of standard on every listed modality.

3. Request for the specific criteria relied upon.

Because the denial appears to rely on MCG criteria that were not identified or provided to me or my surgeon, I am formally requesting, as Molina's own appeals disclosures state I am entitled to do: "The notice will disclose if any internal product rule, protocol, or similar criterion was relied upon to deny the claim or request. Upon request, a copy of the rule, protocol, or similar criterion will be provided to You, free of charge." I am also requesting, per the same disclosure, that Molina "provide an explanation of the scientific or clinical basis for the determination, free of charge," applying that basis to my specific medical circumstances. Please send this information to me and to Dr. Duval's office promptly so that any remaining documentation gap can be identified and addressed within the appeal window.

4. Requested action.

I ask that Molina Healthcare:
(a) Reverse the denial of CPT 29827 based on the conservative treatment already documented above; or, alternatively,
(b) Identify precisely which element of the applicable MCG criteria it contends is undocumented, and provide the criteria text, so that Dr. Duval can submit any additional supporting documentation within the appeal timeframe.

Enclosed with this letter are the following records supporting this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-23 to 2026-07-18, 24 visits)
- Medication/injection records documenting 8 months of NSAID use and the 2026-04-21 corticosteroid injection
- MRI report dated 2026-07-06
- Office examination notes documenting range-of-motion limitation and positive provocative testing
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Duval, [orthopedic surgery / practice name and NPI not in records]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of the review timeline. If this matter qualifies for expedited review due to ongoing pain and functional loss, please treat it accordingly and contact me at the number above.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Rowan Carter
